name: ncr53c8xx_init
prose: Precondition: none; called once at init (__init). Postcondition: it stores the result of spi_attach_transport(&ncr53c8xx_transport_functions) in the global ncr53c8xx_transport_template and returns -ENODEV (-19) if that result is NULL, and 0 otherwise. It takes no lock.
note: ncr53c8xx.c:8400-8406. Contract dropped because the function assigns a global.

name: hw_event_phy_down
prose: Precondition: piomb points to a readable hardware event message whose decoded port_id and phy_id index valid entries of pm8001_ha->port and pm8001_ha->phy. Postcondition: returns nothing. It stores the decoded portstate in port->port_state and clears phy->phy_type, phy->identify.device_type, phy->phy_attached and phy->dev_sas_addr, then switches on portstate: PORT_VALID does nothing more (no log); PORT_IN_RESET only logs and leaves port->port_attached unchanged; PORT_INVALID and PORT_LOSTCOMM log, clear port->port_attached and send a HW_EVENT_PHY_DOWN acknowledgement with pm8001_hw_event_ack_req; PORT_NOT_ESTABLISHED and any unrecognised state log and clear port->port_attached without sending an acknowledgement.
note: reviewer (round 15: PORT_VALID does not log, it only breaks) right, pm8001_hwi.c:3246-3247; round 2 (NOT_ESTABLISHED also clears port_attached) is how the text now reads. Function at 3227-3281.

name: fw_crash_buffer_show
prose: Precondition: cdev is the class device of a megasas host and buf is a writable sysfs buffer of at least PAGE_SIZE bytes; the caller does not hold instance->crashdump_lock. Postcondition: it takes instance->crashdump_lock (a mutex) and releases it on every return. If instance->crash_dump_buf is NULL or fw_crash_state is neither AVAILABLE nor COPYING it logs 'Firmware crash dump is not available' and returns -EINVAL without copying. If fw_crash_buffer_offset is greater than fw_crash_buffer_size * CRASH_DMA_BUF_SIZE it logs an error and returns 0 without copying. Otherwise it copies size bytes into buf and returns size, where size is the smaller of the bytes left in the whole dump after the offset and the bytes left in the current CRASH_DMA_BUF_SIZE chunk, reduced to PAGE_SIZE - 1 if that value is PAGE_SIZE or more; the source is crash_buf[offset / CRASH_DMA_BUF_SIZE] plus offset % CRASH_DMA_BUF_SIZE, and size can be 0.
note: reviewer (round 15: a NULL crash_dump_buf returns -EINVAL without logging or locking) wrong: the mutex is taken at megaraid_sas_base.c:3313 and dev_err is called at 3318 before the -EINVAL return at 3321. Function at 3301-3342.

name: lpfc_debugfs_initialize
prose: Function lpfc_debugfs_initialize(vport) creates the debugfs entries for a vport; with CONFIG_SCSI_LPFC_DEBUG_FS undefined its body is empty. It returns void. If lpfc_debugfs_enable is zero it returns at once. If the global lpfc_debugfs_root is unset it creates the lpfc directory, zeroes lpfc_debugfs_hba_count, and returns after a warning if the result IS_ERR. It sets lpfc_debugfs_start_time to jiffies if it was zero. If phba->hba_debugfs_root is unset it sets pport_setup = true, creates the fn<brd_no> directory, zeroes phba->debugfs_vport_count (return after a warning on IS_ERR), increments lpfc_debugfs_hba_count, creates the files multixripools, cgn_buffer, rx_monitor, ras_log, hbqinfo (plus lockstat only if LPFC_HDWQ_LOCK_STAT), dumpHBASlim and dumpHostSlim only when sli_rev < LPFC_SLI_REV4, and the InjErr and read/write guard/app/ref inject files (setting lpfc_injerr_lba to LPFC_INJERR_LBA_OFF). It rounds lpfc_debugfs_max_slow_ring_trc down to a power of two when it is nonzero and not one (with a pr_info), creates slow_ring_trace, and if phba->slow_ring_trc is unset allocates it with kcalloc; on failure it logs 0416 and jumps to out, which returns without creating the vport directory or the later files. It then creates nvmeio_trc, zeroes nvmeio_trc_cnt, and if lpfc_debugfs_max_nvmeio_trc is nonzero rounds it down to a power of two, sets nvmeio_trc_size, kzallocs nvmeio_trc and on success sets nvmeio_trc_on = 1 and nvmeio_trc_output_idx = 0; if the allocation fails (log 0576) or the maximum is zero it sets nvmeio_trc_size, nvmeio_trc_on, nvmeio_trc_output_idx to 0 and nvmeio_trc to NULL. Then, for every call, if vport->vport_debugfs_root is unset it creates the vport<vpi> directory (return after a warning on IS_ERR) and increments phba->debugfs_vport_count. It rounds lpfc_debugfs_max_disc_trc down to a power of two when nonzero, then always kzallocs vport->disc_trc (on failure logs 0418 and jumps to out, returning without creating the vport files), zeroes disc_trc_cnt, and creates discovery_trace, nodelist, nvmestat, scsistat, ioktime and hdwqstat. If pport_setup is false, or sli_rev < LPFC_SLI_REV4, it returns. Otherwise it creates the iDiag directory if phba->idiag_root is unset (clearing the global idiag state when it does) and the pciCfg, barAcc, queInfo, queAcc, drbAcc, ctlAcc and mbxAcc files, and extAcc when sli4_hba.extents_in_use is set. Errors from debugfs_create_file are not checked.
note: slice cut the head and the packet name is wrong: the real function is lpfc_debugfs_initialize (lpfc_debugfs.c:6063-6380), there is no lpfc_debugfs_setup; pport_setup is a local variable, not a parameter as the old prose said. Whole function read. Old prose claim that disc_trc_cnt is zeroed and the nvmeio reset on failure is right; added the early returns and the two goto out paths that skip later entries.

name: lpfc_els_unsol_buffer
prose: Function lpfc_els_unsol_buffer(phba, pring, vport, elsiocb) handles one received unsolicited ELS frame and returns void. If vport is NULL or elsiocb->cmd_dmabuf is NULL it goes to dropit. Otherwise it takes payload from the buffer, sets payload_len (SLI4: wcqe total_data_placed; else the SLI3 acc_len), reads the ULP status and the first command word, reposts one SLI-3 buffer with lpfc_sli3_post_buffer when HBQ is not enabled, and reads the DID. It goes to dropit if the ULP status is nonzero, lpfc_els_chk_latt reports a link attention, FC_UNLOADING is set, or FC_DISC_DELAYED is set and the command is not PLOGI. It finds the node by DID; if none exists it creates one with lpfc_nlp_init (failure goes to dropit), sets it to NLP_STE_NPR_NODE, marks newnode and sets NLP_FABRIC for a fabric DID; if the node is NLP_STE_UNUSED_NODE it sets NPR state and newnode. It increments elsRcvFrame. If NLP_IN_DEV_LOSS is set on the node it puts the node (only when newnode) and goes to dropit. Then it takes a node reference with lpfc_nlp_get into elsiocb->ndlp (NULL goes to dropit) and sets elsiocb->vport. If the port_state is below LPFC_FABRIC_CFG_LINK, the command is not FLOGI, and it is not a PLOGI with FC_PT2PT set, it sets LSRJT_LOGICAL_BSY and goes to lsrjt. Otherwise it dispatches on the ELS command: PLOGI (confirms the nport; on SLI4 point-to-point updates fc_myDID/fc_prevDID; rejects with LSRJT_UNABLE_TPC if FC_DISC_DELAYED is set, or if port_state is below LPFC_DISC_AUTH and either the port is not point-to-point or FC_PT2PT_PLOGI is set; else runs the state machine with NLP_EVT_RCV_PLOGI), FLOGI (if port_state >= LPFC_LOCAL_CFG_LINK, FC_PT2PT is set and rcv_flogi_cnt >= 1 it rejects with LSRJT_LOGICAL_BSY and sets init_link; else calls lpfc_els_rcv_flogi, and unless a deferred flogi acc is pending removes a new node with NLP_EVT_DEVICE_RM), LOGO, PRLO, ADISC and PDISC (rejected with LSRJT_UNABLE_TPC when port_state is below LPFC_DISC_AUTH, otherwise passed to the state machine), PRLI/NVMEPRLI (rejected only when port_state < LPFC_DISC_AUTH and FC_FABRIC is set), LCB, RDP, RSCN, FARPR, FARP, FAN, LIRR, RLS, RPL, RNID, RTV, RRQ, ECHO (handled by their lpfc_els_rcv_* helper, several of which then remove a new node), REC (rejected with LSRJT_UNABLE_TPC and exp INVALID_OX_RX), FPIN, EDC, RDF (rejected with LSRJT_PROTOCOL_ERR unless the DID is Fabric_Cntl_DID), and any other command (rejected with LSRJT_CMD_UNSUPPORTED, removing a new node). At lsrjt, if rjt_err is set it sends lpfc_els_rsp_reject and removes a new node. After the switch it puts the node reference with lpfc_nlp_put(elsiocb->ndlp); if init_link is set it allocates a mailbox from mbox_mem_pool (returning if that fails), builds an init-link command, issues it with MBX_NOWAIT and frees the mailbox if the issue returns MBX_NOT_FINISHED; then it returns. The dropit label is reached only by the goto paths above: it logs 0111 when vport is non-NULL and not unloading and increments phba->fc_stat.elsRcvDrop; in the dropit paths no reference is kept (elsiocb->ndlp is set only after the lpfc_nlp_get that succeeds).
note: slice cut the head: the real function is lpfc_els_unsol_buffer (lpfc_els.c:10314-10775). Reviewer r15 right: a PLOGI below LPFC_DISC_AUTH is not always rejected, in point-to-point mode it is passed on unless FC_PT2PT_PLOGI is set (10445-10452). Read in full (switch bodies for the simple helper-only cases skimmed). Caveat: the old prose' 'silently drops ... NLP_IN_DEV_LOSS'/'lpfc_nlp_get failure' list is right, but dropit also logs at KERN_ERR and counts elsRcvDrop, which is stated here.

name: lpfc_issue_els_prli
prose: Function lpfc_issue_els_prli(vport, ndlp, retry) sends PRLI ELS commands to a remote port and returns 0 or 1 (1 on any failure shown below). Before sending it, on SLI4 with FC_RSCN_MODE set and vport->nvmei_support it ORs NLP_FC4_NVME into ndlp->nlp_fc4_type; it copies nlp_fc4_type into local_nlp_type; and it clears the FCP and NVME target/initiator bits of nlp_type, NLP_FCP_2_DEVICE in nlp_fcp_info, the NLP_FIRSTBURST and NLP_NPR_2B_DISC flag bits, and sets nvme_fb_size to 0. At send_next_prli it picks FCP PRLI if local_nlp_type has NLP_FC4_FCP, else NVME PRLI if it has NLP_FC4_NVME, else logs and returns 1. On SLI3 when nlp_fc4_type is exactly NLP_FC4_NVME it logs, runs the state machine with NLP_EVT_DEVICE_RM and returns 1. It allocates the IOCB with lpfc_prep_els_iocb (NULL returns 1), builds the FCP PRLI payload (FC-TAPE bits when feaLevelHigh >= 2, estabImagePair, readXferRdyDis, writeXferRdyDis when cfg_first_burst_size is set, initiator function, flag LPFC_PRLI_FCP_REQ) or the NVME PRLI payload (nsler/conf, fba when cfg_nvme_enable_fb and not nvmet_support, target/disc or init/conf bits, word1 and word4 converted to big endian, flag LPFC_PRLI_NVME_REQ), and clears that type's bit in local_nlp_type. It then increments fc_stat.elsXmitPRLI, sets the completion handler to lpfc_cmpl_els_prli and takes a node reference with lpfc_nlp_get into elsiocb->ndlp; if that fails it frees the IOCB and returns 1. It issues the IOCB on LPFC_ELS_RING; on IOCB_ERROR it frees the IOCB, puts the node reference and returns 1. After a successful issue it sets NLP_PRLI_SND and, under ndlp->lock, increments vport->fc_prli_sent and ndlp->fc4_prli_sent. If the adapter is SLI4 and local_nlp_type still has an FCP or NVME bit set it loops to send_next_prli (so a later iteration can still return 1 after an earlier PRLI was already sent); otherwise it returns 0. On SLI3 it therefore sends only one PRLI even if both FC4 types are set.
note: slice cut the head: the real function is lpfc_issue_els_prli (lpfc_els.c:2481-2657). Reviewer r15 right: with SLI3 and both FCP and NVME set only the first PRLI (FCP) is sent and 0 is returned (2652-2656). Full function read.

name: lpfc_els_retry
prose: Function lpfc_els_retry(phba, cmdiocb, rspiocb) decides whether a failed ELS command should be reissued and returns 1 if it has started a retry (immediate or delayed) and 0 if it has not. It takes the original command word from cmdiocb->cmd_dmabuf when present, and the DID from ndlp when ndlp exists, else from the response and ndlp is looked up with lpfc_findnode_did; if there is still no ndlp and the command is not PLOGI it returns 0. It classifies the failure by the ULP status (and for IOSTAT_LOCAL_REJECT the IOERR parameter, for IOSTAT_LS_RJT the LS_RJT reason, explanation and vendor code), which sets retry, delay, maxretry or link_reset; for the cases shown, for example IOERR_NO_RESOURCES retries until cmdiocb->retry exceeds 100, ILLEGAL_COMMAND until it exceeds 2, and the LS_RJT cases retry only for particular command and reason combinations (the classification switch was read as a control-flow outline, not line by line). If link_reset is set it calls lpfc_link_reset: nonzero sets retry = 1 and delay = 100 and goes to out_retry, zero returns 1. A command to FDMI_DID sets retry = 1. A FLOGI that is not on a loop topology and not a lost-link error sets retry = 1 with maxretry 0 (or 2 in loopback mode) and delay 5000 if retry >= 100 or 1000 if retry >= 32; an FDISC that is not a lost-link error sets retry = 1, maxretry = vport->cfg_devloss_tmo and delay = 1000. It increments cmdiocb->retry; if maxretry is nonzero and retry has reached it, it counts elsRetryExceeded and clears retry; if FC_UNLOADING is set it clears retry. At out_retry, if retry is set: for PLOGI or FDISC while FCF_DISCOVERY is set it returns 0 without retrying; it may reset the discovery timer (PLOGI or ADISC unless the failure was IOERR_NO_RESOURCES, with the timer pending or FC_RSCN_MODE set); it increments elsXmitRetry; if ndlp exists and delay is nonzero it stores nlp_retry, arms nlp_delayfunc with mod_timer for delay ms, sets NLP_DELAY_TMO, records nlp_prev_state, sets the node state to NLP_STE_PRLI_ISSUE for PRLI or NVMEPRLI and to NLP_STE_NPR_NODE for any other command except ADISC (for a delayed ADISC nlp_state is not changed), stores nlp_last_elscmd and returns 1. Without a delay it reissues the command immediately with the matching lpfc_issue_els_* function (FLOGI, FDISC, PLOGI, ADISC, PRLI/NVMEPRLI, LOGO), setting the node state to the corresponding *_ISSUE state first for those that have a node, and returns 1 regardless of whether the reissue succeeded. If retry is not set or the command is a type not in that switch, it logs and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head: the real function is lpfc_els_retry (lpfc_els.c:4575-5066). Reviewer r15 right: the delayed-retry path sets NPR or PRLI_ISSUE state for every command except ADISC, so a deferred ADISC leaves nlp_state unchanged (5003-5011). Large function: the final part (4912-5066) and the head were read line by line; the IOSTAT/IOERR/LSRJT classification switch (4618-4910) was read only as a control-flow outline, so the detailed per-case retry/delay values are summarised, not enumerated.

name: lpfc_cmpl_els_flogi
prose: Function lpfc_cmpl_els_flogi(phba, cmdiocb, rspiocb) is the completion handler for a FLOGI ELS command; it returns void. It works with ndlp = cmdiocb->ndlp. Every path that leaves through the out label does: if no FLOGI retry was started (flogi_in_retry false) clear HBA_FLOGI_OUTSTANDING, free the command IOCB with lpfc_els_free_iocb, and drop one node reference with lpfc_nlp_put(ndlp). Paths: (1) if lpfc_els_chk_latt reports a link attention, then, only when NLP_IN_DEV_LOSS and NLP_DROPPED are both clear and the node is not SCSI_XPT_REGD, it sets NLP_DROPPED and puts the node (an extra put); then goto out. (2) If the ULP status is nonzero (failure): on SLI4 with FIP support it may pick the next FCF index (lpfc_sli4_fcf_rr_next_index_get) and, depending on link state and CVL attention counters, either go to stop_rr_fcf_flogi or goto out (this part was read as an outline); then it calls lpfc_els_retry; if that returns nonzero (retry started) it calls lpfc_check_nlp_post_devloss, sets flogi_in_retry and goes to out, keeping HBA_FLOGI_OUTSTANDING. Otherwise it sets NLP_DROPPED and puts the node under the same three-way condition as in (1), and if the failure is not LOCAL_REJECT with IOERR_LOOP_OPEN_FAILURE it goes to flogifail. For a loop-open failure it clears FC_FABRIC, FC_PUBLIC_LOOP and FC_PT2PT_NO_NVME, sets cfg_discovery_threads to LPFC_MAX_DISC_THREADS when alpa_map[0] is 0, and on SLI4 with FC_VFI_REGISTERED either unregisters the FCF (if the topology changed) or all RPIs, issues lpfc_issue_reg_vfi unless the error is a lost link, and goes to out; in the other cases it goes to flogifail. (3) On success it clears FC_VPORT_CVL_RCVD and FC_VPORT_LOGO_RCVD, takes the response payload buffer; if there is no response buffer or it is not an ELS accept it goes to out. It handles VMID and priority tagging, then if port_state == LPFC_FLOGI it calls lpfc_cmpl_els_flogi_fabric when the F_Port bit is set, lpfc_cmpl_els_flogi_nport when it is clear and the adapter is not in FCoE mode, and in the FCoE-with-cleared-fabric-bit case logs error 2831, puts the node, clears FCF_DISCOVERY (under hbalock), FCF_RR_INPROG and HBA_DEVLOSS_TMO, resets fcf_redisc_attempted and goes to out. If the helper returned 0 it clears FCF_DISCOVERY, FCF_RR_INPROG and HBA_DEVLOSS_TMO, resets fcf_redisc_attempted and goes to out; if the helper returned nonzero it falls through to flogifail. If instead port_state > LPFC_FLOGI with FC_PT2PT set and the F_Port bit clear it goes to out. (4) flogifail: clears FCF_DISCOVERY under hbalock; if the status is not a lost-link error it runs lpfc_disc_list_loopmap and lpfc_disc_start, else, unless the failure was LOCAL_REJECT with SLI_ABORTED or SLI_DOWN or the link state is already LPFC_CLEAR_LA, it calls lpfc_issue_clear_la. It then reaches out.
note: Reviewers: original right (the extra put is conditional on NLP_IN_DEV_LOSS/NLP_DROPPED/SCSI_XPT_REGD being clear, 940-945, 1023-1028, not unconditional); r15 mixed: when lpfc_cmpl_els_flogi_fabric/nport return nonzero control falls through to flogifail (the 'if (!rc)' block is skipped, 1165-1180), so r15 is wrong for that case, but the FCoE cleared-fabric-bit branch does drop the node ref and goto out (1156-1163). Part read as an outline only: the FIP/FCF round-robin block (964-995) and the status-error details. Source of the head (920-935) and tail read line by line.

name: lpfc_hb_timeout_handler
prose: Function lpfc_hb_timeout_handler(phba) is the HBA heartbeat timer handler; it returns void. If phba->cfg_xri_rebalancing is set it first calls lpfc_hb_mxp_handler. It then walks the vport work array calling lpfc_rcv_seq_check_edtov and lpfc_fdmi_change_check on each vport, and destroys the array. If the link_state is LPFC_HBA_ERROR, or FC_UNLOADING or FC_OFFLINE_MODE is set on the physical port, it returns at this point without touching the ELS buffer list and without re-arming hb_tmofunc. Otherwise, if phba->elsbuf_cnt is nonzero and equal to elsbuf_prev_cnt, it moves the whole elsbuf list to a local list under hbalock, zeroes elsbuf_cnt and elsbuf_prev_cnt, and frees each buffer with lpfc_mbuf_free and kfree. It then sets elsbuf_prev_cnt = elsbuf_cnt. The timer interval tmo is chosen as follows. If cfg_enable_hba_heartbeat is set: if the last completion is less than LPFC_HB_MBOX_INTERVAL seconds old it uses tmo = LPFC_HB_MBOX_TIMEOUT seconds when HBA_HBEAT_INP is set or LPFC_HB_MBOX_INTERVAL otherwise; else if a heartbeat is still outstanding (HBA_HBEAT_INP) it logs and uses the TIMEOUT value; else, when no mailbox is active and the mailbox queue is empty, it calls lpfc_issue_hb_mbox (nonzero result: tmo = INTERVAL seconds and go to the re-arm; zero: skipped_hb = 0), and when the mailbox is busy it logs if last_completion_time is not newer than skipped_hb, else records skipped_hb = jiffies; in these non-error cases tmo is the TIMEOUT value. If cfg_enable_hba_heartbeat is not set: when HBA_HBEAT_TMO is set it calls lpfc_issue_hb_mbox (tmo = INTERVAL on failure, TIMEOUT on success), otherwise tmo = INTERVAL. Every path that reaches the end calls mod_timer(&phba->hb_tmofunc, jiffies + tmo ms), including the lpfc_issue_hb_mbox failure path; only the early return for error, unloading or offline skips the re-arm.
note: slice cut the head: the real function is lpfc_hb_timeout_handler (lpfc_init.c:1508-1619). Reviewers: original right (early return before elsbuf/heartbeat), r2 right (the cfg_enable_hba_heartbeat guard), r15 mixed/wrong: re-arm is NOT skipped on issue failure, it uses INTERVAL and goes to out (1586-1589, 1618); the re-arm is skipped only on the early return at 1534. Full function read.

name: lpfc_sli_driver_resource_setup
prose: Static function lpfc_sli_driver_resource_setup(phba) sets up driver resources for an SLI-3 or SLI-2 adapter and returns 0 or a negative errno. Steps in order: it sets up the fcp_poll_timer with lpfc_poll_timeout, sets work_ha_mask to HA_ERATT|HA_MBATT|HA_LATT plus the ELS ring receive bits, calls lpfc_get_cfgparam, and calls lpfc_setup_driver_resource_phase1; if that returns nonzero the function returns -ENODEV. If phba->sli.sli3_ring is unset it allocates it with kcalloc (LPFC_SLI3_MAX_RING rings); if the pointer is still NULL it returns -ENOMEM. It sets the scatter/gather sizes: entry_sz is sizeof(struct sli4_sge) on SLI4 else sizeof(struct ulp_bde64); with cfg_enable_bg it sets cfg_sg_dma_buf_size from LPFC_MAX_SG_SEG_CNT entries, caps cfg_sg_seg_cnt at LPFC_MAX_SG_SEG_CNT_DIF and sets cfg_total_seg_cnt = LPFC_MAX_SG_SEG_CNT; otherwise it sets cfg_sg_dma_buf_size from cfg_sg_seg_cnt + 2 entries and cfg_total_seg_cnt = cfg_sg_seg_cnt + 2. It sets max_vpi = LPFC_MAX_VPI and max_vports = 0, then calls lpfc_sli_setup and lpfc_sli_queue_init. If lpfc_mem_alloc(phba, BPL_ALIGN_SZ) fails it returns -ENOMEM directly, with no further cleanup in this function (the sli3_ring allocation is not freed here). It creates the lpfc_sg_dma_buf_pool dma pool (failure: goto fail_free_mem) and the lpfc_cmd_rsp_buf_pool (failure: goto fail_free_dma_buf_pool). If cfg_sriov_nr_virtfn > 0 it calls lpfc_sli_probe_sriov_nr_virtfn; a nonzero result is logged and cfg_sriov_nr_virtfn is reset to 0 but the function still continues. It then returns 0. The error labels run in sequence: fail_free_dma_buf_pool destroys the sg dma buf pool and sets it to NULL, fail_free_mem calls lpfc_mem_free, and then it returns -ENOMEM.
note: slice cut the head: the real function is lpfc_sli_driver_resource_setup (lpfc_init.c:7757-7894). Reviewer r15 right: the lpfc_mem_alloc failure return at 7848-7849 is a direct -ENOMEM with no cleanup. Full function read.

name: lpfc_mem_alloc
prose: Function lpfc_mem_alloc(phba, align) allocates the HBA's DMA pools and memory pools and returns 0 on success or -ENOMEM. It allocates, in order: the lpfc_mbuf_pool dma pool; the lpfc_mbuf_safety_pool.elements array with kmalloc_array of LPFC_MBUF_POOL_SIZE entries, then fills each element with dma_pool_alloc from the mbuf pool while counting max_count and current_count; the mbox_mem_pool, nlp_mem_pool mempools. On SLI4 it then creates rrq_pool, lpfc_hrb_pool and lpfc_drb_pool and sets lpfc_hbq_pool to NULL; otherwise it creates lpfc_hbq_pool and sets hrb and drb pools to NULL. If cfg_EnableXLane it creates device_data_mem_pool, else sets it to NULL. It returns 0 after all of these succeed. On a failure it jumps to the matching label and releases what was created before it, in reverse order: drb pool, hrb pool, rrq pool, nlp pool, mbox pool (each destroyed and set to NULL), then the individual mbuf elements already allocated (while (i--)) and the elements array with kfree, then the mbuf pool (set to NULL), and returns -ENOMEM. Details of the cleanup: the elements pointer and the max_count and current_count fields are not reset after the failure; early failures (for example the first dma_pool_create or the kmalloc_array) skip the later destroy calls; on an SLI3 adapter a failure of the device_data_mem_pool allocation goes to the drb-pool label and does not destroy lpfc_hbq_pool, which stays allocated; a failure of lpfc_hbq_pool creation jumps to the nlp pool label. The function takes no locks and allocates with GFP_KERNEL.
note: Reviewers all right against lpfc_mem.c:108-211: r1 (elements not NULLed, counts not reset: 205 kfree only), r2 (SLI3 device_data pool failure leaves lpfc_hbq_pool: no destroy at 186-208), r15 (early failures skip later destroys). Full function read.

name: lpfc_cmpl_prli_prli_issue
prose: Static function lpfc_cmpl_prli_prli_issue(vport, ndlp, arg, evt) handles the completion of a solicited PRLI while the node is in PRLI_ISSUE. arg is the command iocb and its rsp_iocb is the response. It reads the ULP status and calls lpfc_check_elscmpl_iocb; the result is taken as an FCP PRLI response if cmd_flag has LPFC_PRLI_FCP_REQ, or an NVME PRLI response if it has LPFC_PRLI_NVME_REQ. Paths: (1) ULP status nonzero: if the vport is an NPIV port with cfg_restrict_login it goes to out (LOGO) without clearing any FC4 type or changing the state; otherwise it clears NLP_FC4_FCP from nlp_fc4_type for an FCP request or NLP_FC4_NVME for an NVME request and goes to out_err. (2) FCP response with prliType PRLI_FCP_TYPE: acc_imode_sps is set when the accept code is PRLI_INV_SRV_PARM, the initiator bit is set and target and estabImagePair are clear; when the accept code is PRLI_REQ_EXECUTED or acc_imode_sps, it sets NLP_FCP_INITIATOR and/or NLP_FCP_TARGET in nlp_type from the response (NLP_FIRSTBURST flag when target and writeXferRdyDis), and NLP_FCP_2_DEVICE in nlp_fcp_info when Retry is set. (3) NVME response whose accept code is PRLI_REQ_EXECUTED and type code PRLI_NVME_TYPE: sets NLP_NVME_INITIATOR when the init bit is set; sets NLP_NVME_NSLER in nlp_nvme_info when phba->nsler and the nsler and conf bits are set, and clears that bit otherwise; when the target bit is set it sets NLP_NVME_TARGET (plus NLP_NVME_DISCOVERY when the disc bit is set) and, only when the fba bit is 1, cfg_nvme_enable_fb is set and not nvmet_support, it sets NLP_FIRSTBURST and nvme_fb_size (shifted by LPFC_NVME_FB_SHIFT, or LPFC_NVME_MAX_FB when the field is 0). A response that matches neither case leaves nlp_type unchanged. (4) After that, if the node is not an FCP target and the vport is an NPIV port with cfg_restrict_login, it logs, issues lpfc_issue_els_logo(vport, ndlp, 0) and returns ndlp->nlp_state without changing the state. (5) At out_err: only if ndlp->fc4_prli_sent is 0 (this function does not decrement it) it sets nlp_prev_state to NLP_STE_PRLI_ISSUE and moves the node to NLP_STE_MAPPED_NODE when it has an FCP or NVME target type, else to NLP_STE_UNMAPPED_NODE when it has an initiator type (no change if neither); otherwise it logs that PRLIs are still outstanding. Every path returns ndlp->nlp_state, read after any state change.

name: lpfc_rcv_padisc
prose: Static function lpfc_rcv_padisc(vport, ndlp, cmdiocb) handles a received PDISC or ADISC and returns 1 (accepted) or 0 (rejected). It reads the first word of the request from cmdiocb->cmd_dmabuf and takes the node and port names from the ADISC payload (cmd == ELS_CMD_ADISC) or from the service parameters otherwise. If the ULP status of cmdiocb is 0 and lpfc_check_adisc accepts the names: on SLI4, when NLP_RPI_REGISTERED is set on the node, it kmallocs a copy of the iocb (GFP_KERNEL); if the copy succeeds it stores the command in drvrTimeout and calls lpfc_sli4_resume_rpi with lpfc_mbx_cmpl_resume_rpi, kfree's the copy if that call returns nonzero (no ACC is sent in this case), and in either case goes to out without sending the ACC itself (the ACC is sent from the resume completion). In every other accepted case (not SLI4, RPI not registered, or the iocb allocation failed) it sends the ACC immediately: lpfc_els_rsp_adisc_acc for ADISC, else lpfc_els_rsp_acc with ELS_CMD_PLOGI. At out, if the node type has an FCP or NVME target bit, the node state is not already NLP_STE_MAPPED_NODE and NLP_NPR_ADISC is not set, it moves the node to NLP_STE_MAPPED_NODE; then it returns 1. If the status is nonzero or lpfc_check_adisc rejects the names, it builds an LS_RJT (LSRJT_UNABLE_TPC, LSEXP_SPARM_OPTIONS) and sends it with lpfc_els_rsp_reject, arms nlp_delayfunc for 1000 ms, sets NLP_DELAY_TMO, sets nlp_last_elscmd = ELS_CMD_PLOGI, records nlp_prev_state = nlp_state, and returns 0 (the node state itself is not changed in this path).

Reviewers: original right (resume only when NLP_RPI_REGISTERED, 777); r2 right (a failing lpfc_sli4_resume_rpi is only kfree'd, no immediate ACC, 788-794); r15 wrong: the SLI4 resume path does 'goto out' (794), and the MAPPED_NODE update is after the out label (815-819), so it is reached on that path. Full function read.

name: lpfc_nvme_fcp_io_submit
prose: Static function lpfc_nvme_fcp_io_submit(pnvme_lport, pnvme_rport, hw_queue_handle, pnvme_fcreq) is the NVMe-FC transport hook that submits one FCP request; it returns 0 on success or a negative errno. Early failure returns (each increments a counter in lport where noted): lport private data NULL gives -EINVAL; hw_queue_handle NULL gives -EBUSY (xmt_fcp_err); FC_UNLOADING set or HBA_IOQ_FLUSH set gives -ENODEV (xmt_fcp_err); NULL fcreq private data gives -EINVAL (xmt_fcp_err); rport->ndlp NULL gives -EBUSY (xmt_fcp_err); an NVME-target node that is not in NLP_STE_MAPPED_NODE gives -EBUSY (xmt_fcp_bad_ndlp). All of these leave through out_fail and return ret without calling lpfc_update_cmf_cmpl. A keep-alive admin command on queue 0 with no scatter list sets expedite. When congestion management is active and the request is a read with a payload, lpfc_update_cmf_cmd failing gives -EBUSY through out_fail. If ndlp qdepth limiting applies and cmd_pending has reached cmd_qdepth (and not expedite) it returns -EBUSY (xmt_fcp_qdepth) through out_fail1; the index idx is chosen from the queue handle or the CPU map; if lpfc_get_nvme_buf returns NULL it returns -EBUSY (xmt_fcp_noxri) through out_fail1. out_fail1 calls lpfc_update_cmf_cmpl(phba, LPFC_CGN_NOT_SENT, payload_length, NULL) and returns ret. After a buffer is obtained it fills in the buffer, optionally sets a VMID tag, calls lpfc_nvme_prep_io_cmd and lpfc_nvme_prep_io_dma; if the DMA prep returns nonzero it returns -ENOMEM (xmt_fcp_err) after out_free_nvme_buf. It then calls lpfc_sli4_issue_wqe; if that returns nonzero it increments xmt_fcp_wqerr and goes to out_free_nvme_buf, returning the wqe issue error value unchanged. out_free_nvme_buf decrements the matching cstat counter (output, input or control requests), releases the buffer with lpfc_release_nvme_buf, then falls into out_fail1. On success it keeps the private XRI pool above the low watermark when cfg_xri_rebalancing is set, updates debugfs statistics if enabled, and returns 0 with the WQE queued and the buffer owned by the I/O.

name: lpfc_nvme_fcp_abort
prose: Static function lpfc_nvme_fcp_abort(pnvme_lport, pnvme_rport, hw_queue_handle, pnvme_fcreq) is the transport hook that aborts one outstanding NVMe FCP request; it returns void and reports nothing to the caller. It dereferences pnvme_lport and pnvme_fcreq without a NULL check, and pnvme_rport (for port_id, used in log and trace arguments) without a check. It returns silently when: the lport private data is NULL, hw_queue_handle is NULL (logged), freqpriv is NULL, FC_UNLOADING is set, freqpriv->nvme_buf is NULL (logged), the buffer's nvmeCmd is NULL (logged), or HBA_IOQ_FLUSH is set (logged). Otherwise it takes buf_lock with spin_lock_irqsave and then hbalock. It skips the abort (unlocking both and returning) when the buffer's nvmeCmd is not pnvme_fcreq (logged) or when LPFC_IO_ON_TXCMPLQ is not set on the iocb (logged). Only after those two checks does it increment lport->xmt_fcp_abort and trace the abort. If LPFC_DRIVER_ABORTED is already set it logs that an abort is pending and skips (unlocking and returning). Otherwise it calls lpfc_sli4_issue_abort_iotag with lpfc_nvme_abort_fcreq_cmpl as the completion, releases both locks, calls lpfc_issue_hb_tmo(phba), and if the abort issue returned anything other than WQE_SUCCESS it logs the failure and returns; on success it logs that the transport abort was issued and returns. The function itself neither completes nor frees the request.

Reviewers all right: original (the failed-issue path at 1974-1980 only logs), r2 (hw_queue_handle and freqpriv are checked, not preconditions), r15 (pnvme_rport is used without a check; xmt_fcp_abort is incremented only after the mismatch and not-queued skips, 1949). name: lpfc_nvme_unsol_ls_issue_abort
prose: Function lpfc_nvme_unsol_ls_issue_abort(phba, ctxp, sid, xri) issues an abort for an unsolicited NVMe LS exchange and returns 0 or 1. If the exchange is in state LPFC_NVME_STE_LS_RCV with entry_cnt 1, or LPFC_NVME_STE_LS_RSP with entry_cnt 2, it sets the state to LPFC_NVME_STE_LS_ABORT and increments entry_cnt; for any other state and count it logs and sets the state to LPFC_NVME_STE_LS_ABORT without changing entry_cnt (so any state is accepted). If nvmet_support and phba->targetport are set it takes tgtp from the target port private data. If ctxp->wqeq is NULL it gets an iocbq with lpfc_sli_get_iocbq; if that returns NULL it logs, kfree's ctxp and returns 0. It then calls lpfc_nvmet_unsol_issue_abort(phba, ctxp, sid, xri); a return value of 0 from that helper is treated as failure (rc = WQE_BUSY, goto out). Otherwise, under hbalock (irqsave) it sets the abort wqe's completion to lpfc_nvmet_xmt_ls_abort_cmp, sets LPFC_IO_NVME_LS in its cmd_flag and calls lpfc_sli4_issue_wqe; if that returns WQE_SUCCESS it increments tgtp->xmt_abort_unsol (when tgtp is set) and returns 0. In all other cases (helper returned 0 or the wqe issue failed) it goes through out: it increments tgtp->xmt_abort_rsp_error when tgtp is set, clears the abort wqe's rsp_dmabuf and bpl_dmabuf pointers, releases the iocbq with lpfc_sli_release_iocbq and returns 1. The out path does not clear any flags in ctxp and does not free ctxp.

Reviewers all right: original (any state is accepted; helper result 0 leads to return 1, 3587-3590), r15 (the out label only counts the error, clears the two dmabuf pointers and releases the iocbq, it does not clear flags, 3602-3610). Full function read.

name: lpfc_bg_err_inject
prose: Static function lpfc_bg_err_inject(phba, sc, reftag, apptag, new_guard) decides whether and how to inject a T10-PI (BlockGuard) error into a command, and returns a flag word rc (0 when nothing is injected). Early return 0: the protection operation of sc is SCSI_PROT_NORMAL; when phba->lpfc_injerr_lba is not LPFC_INJERR_LBA_OFF and falls outside the command's LBA range; when lpfc_injerr_nportid is set and differs from the node's DID; or when the injection WWPN is set and differs from the node's port name. When a protection scatterlist exists it points src at the tuple at the block offset of the injection LBA (clamped to the entry count) and takes lpfc_cmd from sc->host_scribble. Then three independent sections run: if reftag is non-NULL, the write-reference counter lpfc_injerr_wref_cnt (for SCSI_PROT_WRITE_PASS with a tuple it saves the original reference tag in lpfc_cmd and overwrites ref_tag with 0xDEADBEEF; for WRITE_PASS without a tuple or WRITE_INSERT it only counts) is decremented and rc is set to BG_ERR_TGT | BG_ERR_CHECK, or BG_ERR_INIT for WRITE_STRIP; the read-reference counter lpfc_injerr_rref_cnt, when nonzero for a READ_INSERT, READ_STRIP or READ_PASS op, is decremented and rc set to BG_ERR_INIT; if apptag is non-NULL the same pattern applies to lpfc_injerr_wapp_cnt (overwriting app_tag with 0xDEAD for WRITE_PASS with a tuple) and lpfc_injerr_rapp_cnt; if new_guard is nonzero, lpfc_injerr_wgrd_cnt gives rc = BG_ERR_CHECK (WRITE_PASS only) | BG_ERR_TGT | BG_ERR_SWAP for WRITE_PASS and WRITE_INSERT, or BG_ERR_INIT | BG_ERR_SWAP for WRITE_STRIP, and lpfc_injerr_rgrd_cnt gives BG_ERR_INIT | BG_ERR_SWAP for the read ops. Each time a counter reaches zero it clears lpfc_injerr_nportid, sets lpfc_injerr_lba to LPFC_INJERR_LBA_OFF and zeroes lpfc_injerr_wwpn. Only the guard WRITE_PASS case ORs into rc; every other injection assigns rc, so when several sections match in one call the later assignment overwrites the earlier value (the counters of all matching sections are still decremented). The function returns rc.

Prose checked against the code but the log-message lines and several comment blocks were skipped; the repeated counter blocks were read once and verified by pattern.

name: lpfc_new_scsi_buf_s3
prose: Static function lpfc_new_scsi_buf_s3(vport, num_to_alloc) allocates up to num_to_alloc SCSI I/O buffers for an SLI-3 adapter and returns the number actually created (bcnt, possibly less than requested, possibly 0). For each buffer it kzallocs a struct lpfc_io_buf (stop at the first failure); allocates its data area with dma_pool_zalloc from phba->lpfc_sg_dma_buf_pool (on failure it kfree's the buffer and stops); gets an iotag with lpfc_sli_next_iotag (if it returns 0 it frees the dma data and the buffer and stops). On success it marks cur_iocbq with LPFC_IO_FCP, lays out the data area as FCP command, FCP response and scatter-gather list, fills the first two BDEs of the BPL with the command and response DMA addresses, and sets up the iocb: for SLI rev 3 without BlockGuard enabled it uses an immediate BDE for the command and an extended response BDE; otherwise it points the BDL at the BPL (BUFF_TYPE_BLP_64, two BDEs). It sets ulpClass to CLASS3, status to IOSTAT_SUCCESS, io_buf back-pointer, initialises buf_lock and puts the buffer on the free list with lpfc_release_scsi_buf_s3. The function takes no locks itself; the count of created buffers is returned even when an allocation stopped the loop early (partial success is not reported as an error).

name: lpfc_cq_create_set
prose: Function lpfc_cq_create_set(phba, cqp, hdwq, type, subtype) creates a set of completion queues with one SLI4 mailbox command and returns 0 or a negative errno. The count numcq is taken from phba->cfg_nvmet_mrq (it is not a parameter). If cqp or hdwq is NULL or numcq is 0 it returns -ENODEV. It allocates a mailbox from mbox_mem_pool (failure: -ENOMEM) and builds the non-embedded CQ_CREATE_SET config; if lpfc_sli4_config allocated less than the needed length it sets -ENOMEM and goes to out. Every path after the mailbox allocation leaves through out, which frees the mailbox with lpfc_sli4_mbox_cmd_free and returns status. For each index 0..numcq-1 it takes cq = cqp[idx] and eq = hdwq[idx].hba_eq; if either is NULL it sets -ENOMEM and goes to out. For idx 0 it fills the common request fields (page size, page count, numcq, cqav) and the entry-count field: 2048 or 4096 entries use the count word only when cq version is LPFC_Q_CREATE_VERSION_2, any other count falls to the default case, which logs, returns -EINVAL (through out) if entry_count < 256 and otherwise uses the 256 encoding (so entry counts above 1024 that are not handled by version 2 are encoded as 256); counts 256, 512, 1024 use their encodings. For every idx 0..15 it sets that queue's EQ id field in the request; indices above 15 set nothing in the request. It then adds cq to eq->child_list, sets type, subtype, assoc_qid, assoc_qp, host_index, notify_interval, max_proc_limit and chann, zeroes each page of the queue and writes its physical address into the request page array. It issues the mailbox with lpfc_sli_issue_mbox(..., MBX_POLL); if the issue return value or either header status is nonzero it logs and sets -ENXIO, goes to out. It reads the response base id; if it is 0xFFFF it sets -ENXIO. Otherwise it assigns queue_id = base + idx to each cq and raises phba->sli4_hba.cq_max if needed, and returns 0. On the error paths after the loop has started, the queues already added to eq->child_list are not removed again by this function.
note: slice cut the head: the real function is lpfc_cq_create_set (lpfc_sli.c:16421-16648), not lpfc_sli4_cq_create_set; numcq is read from phba->cfg_nvmet_mrq, so the old prose' 'numcq nonzero' precondition was about a parameter that does not exist. Full function read except the 16 repeated per-index bf_set blocks.

name: lpfc_sli4_seq_abort_rsp
prose: Function lpfc_sli4_seq_abort_rsp(vport, fc_hdr, aborted) sends a BLS response (BA_ACC or BA_RJT) for a received ABTS and returns void. Paths: if the link is not up it returns. It reads the source id, OX_ID and RX_ID from fc_hdr and finds the node with lpfc_findnode_did; if there is none it creates one with lpfc_nlp_init (NULL: logs and returns) and enqueues it. It gets an iocbq with lpfc_sli_get_iocbq (NULL: returns, leaving a node created above in place), then takes a node reference with lpfc_nlp_get into ctiocb->ndlp; if that fails it releases the iocbq and returns (again without releasing a node created above). Otherwise it sets the vport, the completion lpfc_sli4_seq_abort_rsp_cmpl and abort_rctl = FC_RCTL_BA_ACC, selects xri as OX_ID when FC_FC_EX_CTX is set in the frame control else RX_ID, and if lpfc_sli4_xri_inrange returns a valid logical xri it calls lpfc_set_rrq_active. It changes the response to BA_RJT (reason FC_BA_RJT_UNABLE, explanation FC_BA_RJT_INV_XID) when FC_FC_EX_CTX is set and the logical xri exceeds lpfc_sli4_get_iocb_cnt, and again when aborted is false. With FC_FC_EX_CTX it sets abort_bls = LPFC_ABTS_UNSOL_RSP and writes RX_ID into the rxid field; otherwise abort_bls = LPFC_ABTS_UNSOL_INT. The oxid field of the BLS response is then written twice, first with oxid and then with rxid, so the final value in that field is rxid. It sets the destination DID, temp RPI and the command CMD_XMIT_BLS_RSP64_CX and issues the iocb on LPFC_ELS_RING; if lpfc_sli_issue_iocb returns IOCB_ERROR it logs, puts the node reference taken above, clears ctiocb->ndlp and releases the iocbq. Finally, on the paths that reach the end (not the early returns), if the node is NLP_STE_UNUSED_NODE, not NLP_DROPPED and has no NVME or SCSI transport registration, it sets NLP_DROPPED and puts the node.

Reviewers: original right (after a newly created ndlp, the ctiocb allocation and nlp_get failures return without releasing it, 19003-19016); r2 right (nlp_get failure releases the iocbq; the reason code is FC_BA_RJT_UNABLE); r15 wrong: the code writes the xmit_bls_rsp64_oxid field twice, first oxid then rxid (19073-19074), so the oxid field is overwritten with rxid; the old prose was correct on that point. Full function read except the logging lines.

name: lpfc_sli4_alloc_extent
prose: Static function lpfc_sli4_alloc_extent(phba, type) allocates resource extents of one type (RPI, VPI, XRI or VFI) from the port and records them; it returns 0 or a negative errno. It calls lpfc_sli4_get_avail_extnt_rsrc (nonzero: returns -EIO), and returns -ENOMEM if the available extent count or size is 0. It allocates a mailbox from mbox_mem_pool (NULL: -ENOMEM) and posts the extent request with lpfc_sli4_cfg_post_extnts (nonzero: rc = -EIO, goto err_exit). After that every path leaves through err_exit, which frees the mailbox with lpfc_sli4_mbox_cmd_free and returns rc. It reads the granted extent count from the embedded or non-embedded response, and computes the id count rsrc_cnt * rsrc_size. In a switch on type it allocates, for RPI, VPI, XRI or VFI respectively, a bitmask array with kcalloc and an id array of uint16_t with kcalloc (this function allocates them, they are not pre-existing): a failure of the first allocation gives -ENOMEM, a failure of the second frees the bitmask just allocated (the pointer is not cleared) and gives -ENOMEM; for XRI it also zeroes xri_used and for RPI sets next_rpi to the id count. For any other type it only clears the local pointers and goes to err_exit with rc still 0 (the value left by the successful post), so an unsupported type returns 0 without allocating or recording anything. Then for each extent it reads its start id from the response, kzallocs an lpfc_rsrc_blks, records the start and size, appends it to the type's block list, sets io_xri_start for the first XRI extent (start plus lpfc_sli4_get_iocb_cnt), and fills the ids array with consecutive ids. If the kzalloc of a block fails it sets -ENOMEM, kfree's the bitmask and id arrays (the pointers in phba are not cleared and blocks already added to the list are not freed here) and goes to err_exit.

Reviewer r15 wrong for this source: the RPI case does call kcalloc for rpi_bmask and rpi_ids (6492-6506), they are not pre-existing; the kfree on a block-allocation failure frees those newly allocated arrays. New finding: the default (unsupported type) case returns rc, which is 0 at that point (6585-6591), despite the comment saying the call fails. Full function read.

name: lpfc_sli_issue_mbox_s3
prose: Function lpfc_sli_issue_mbox_s3(phba, pmbox, flag) is the SLI-3 implementation of mailbox issue (the generic lpfc_sli_issue_mbox only calls the phba->lpfc_sli_issue_mbox pointer); it returns a MBX_* status. It takes hbalock with spin_lock_irqsave. If pmbox is NULL it handles the pending queue: when LPFC_SLI_ASYNC_MBX_BLK is set or the queue is empty it unlocks and returns MBX_SUCCESS, otherwise it takes the next mailbox from the queue (processing_queue = 1). It returns MBX_NOT_FINISHED, through out_not_finished and after unlocking, when: a mailbox with a completion routine (other than the default and wake-wait ones) has no vport; the PCI channel is offline; DEFER_ERATT is set; link_state is LPFC_HBA_ERROR; a non-KILL_BOARD NOWAIT command sees a HC register read failure or the controller not able to take mailbox interrupts; a mailbox is active and flag is MBX_POLL; a mailbox is active but the SLI is not active; or flag is not MBX_POLL and the SLI is not active (with its further condition). If a mailbox is already active (and none of the above) it queues pmbox with lpfc_mbox_put, unlocks and returns MBX_BUSY. Otherwise it marks the mailbox active, arms the mailbox timer, copies the command (and extension data) into the mailbox area (SLI memory when active, SLIM otherwise, special-casing MBX_CONFIG_PORT) and then on flag: MBX_NOWAIT writes CA_MBATT and falls to the end; MBX_POLL writes CA_MBATT, then polls the owner bit, with the lock dropped and retaken every 10 iterations, until the chip releases the mailbox or the timeout passes; a register read failure or the timeout goes to out_not_finished; on completion it reads the response back into pmbox (and the extension area), clears the HA mailbox attention and falls to the end. At the end it unlocks and returns status. In out_not_finished, if the call was processing the queue, it puts the mailbox on the completion queue with lpfc_mbox_cmpl_put; it then returns MBX_NOT_FINISHED.

Large function: read as a control-flow outline with the lock/unlock, goto and return lines, so the exact status values stored in pmbox/status on the success and polling paths and the register-copy details were not verified line by line.

name: mega_build_cmd
prose: Static function mega_build_cmd(adapter, cmd, busy) translates a SCSI command into an SCB for the megaraid mailbox interface; it returns a scb_t pointer or NULL. It decides whether the device channel is logical (adapter->logdrv_chan) and derives channel and target, swapping the boot physical drive target with target 0 when boot_pdrv_enabled. Logical device: a nonzero LUN completes the command with DID_BAD_TARGET (scsi_done) and returns NULL (the LUN must be 0 for logical drives); then it derives ldrv_num with mega_get_ldrv_num and, if it exceeds the maximum (MAX_LOGICAL_DRIVES_40LD or _8LD, plus 0x80 when read_ldidmap is set), completes with DID_BAD_TARGET and returns NULL. Physical device: LUN above 7 completes with DID_BAD_TARGET and returns NULL. For a logical device the SCSI opcode decides: TEST_UNIT_READY completes with DID_OK and returns NULL when there is no clustering support (compile-time MEGA_HAVE_CLUSTERING and adapter->has_cluster), otherwise it builds a cluster reservation-status SCB; MODE_SENSE zeroes cmnd[4] bytes of the first scatterlist buffer, completes with DID_OK and returns NULL; READ_CAPACITY and INQUIRY allocate an SCB and build a passthru on the logical drive (data direction from device), returning the SCB; READ_6/WRITE_6/READ_10/WRITE_10/READ_12/WRITE_12 allocate an SCB and fill the mailbox with the logical drive, read or write command (64-bit variant when has_64bit_addr), LBA and sector count decoded from the CDB, the DMA direction, and the scatter-gather list from mega_build_sglist, returning the SCB; RESERVE_6 and RELEASE_6 build a cluster reserve or release SCB if has_cluster, else complete with DID_BAD_TARGET and return NULL; any other opcode completes with DID_BAD_TARGET and returns NULL. name: megasas_transition_to_ready
prose: Function megasas_transition_to_ready(instance, ocr) drives the firmware toward MFI_STATE_READY and returns 0 or -ENODEV. It reads the firmware status register through instance->instancet->read_fw_status_reg and, while the state (abs_state & MFI_STATE_MASK) is not MFI_STATE_READY, switches on it. MFI_STATE_FAULT: logs the fault; if ocr is nonzero it sets max_wait = MEGASAS_RESET_WAIT_TIME and waits for a state change (no -ENODEV from this case), otherwise it dumps the register set and returns -ENODEV. MFI_STATE_WAIT_HANDSHAKE: writes MFI_INIT_CLEAR_HANDSHAKE|MFI_INIT_HOTPLUG to the doorbell register (skinny 0073/0071 devices or any non-MFI_SERIES adapter) or to inbound_doorbell (other MFI_SERIES), then sets max_wait. MFI_STATE_BOOT_MESSAGE_PENDING: writes MFI_INIT_HOTPLUG to the same two registers by the same rule, then sets max_wait. MFI_STATE_OPERATIONAL: disables interrupts; for skinny or non-MFI_SERIES it writes MFI_RESET_FLAGS to the doorbell register and, for non-MFI_SERIES adapters, polls the doorbell bit 0 up to 10 seconds in 20 ms steps; for other MFI_SERIES it writes MFI_RESET_FLAGS to inbound_doorbell; then sets max_wait. MFI_STATE_UNDEFINED, BB_INIT, FW_INIT, FW_INIT_2, DEVICE_SCAN and FLUSH_CACHE: only set max_wait (no register writes). Any other state logs, dumps the registers and returns -ENODEV. After the switch it polls the status register every 20 ms for up to max_wait * 50 iterations while it is unchanged; if it is still equal to abs_state it logs, dumps the registers and returns -ENODEV; otherwise it updates abs_state and fw_state and loops. When the state is READY it returns 0. It takes no locks.

name: cmd_complete
prose: Static function cmd_complete(ms) handles a command-complete interrupt of the MESH SCSI controller and returns void. It computes seq = use_active_neg plus SEQ_ATN when ms->n_msgout is nonzero and switches on ms->msgphase. msg_out_xxx: sets n_msgin = 0, msgphase = msg_in and falls through. msg_in: calls get_msgin, computes the message length; if fewer bytes than needed have arrived it programs the count and the SEQ_MSGIN sequence; otherwise it sets msgphase = msg_none, calls handle_msgin and start_phase. msg_in_bad: flushes the FIFO and issues a one-byte message-in with ATN. msg_out: starts a one-byte message-out, waits up to about 30 us for REQ; if the interrupt register shows INT_ERROR or INT_EXCEPTION it saves last_n_msgout, zeroes n_msgout and calls handle_error (INT_ERROR) or handle_exception (otherwise) and returns; if REQ is set it writes the last message byte and sets msg_out_last, else it issues message-in with ATN and sets msg_out_xxx. msg_out_last: sets last_n_msgout, zeroes n_msgout, sets msgphase to msg_in if expect_reply else msg_none, calls start_phase. msg_none: switches on ms->phase: idle logs via dumpslog and returns without advancing; selecting builds the IDENTIFY message (plus ABORT when ms->aborting, or an SDTR message when tp->sdtr_state is do_sdtr, setting expect_reply and sdtr_state = sdtr_sent), sets msgphase = msg_out and waits up to 230 us for REQ; dataing returns after start_phase when ms->dma_count is nonzero, otherwise clears the sequence and interrupt registers and calls halt_dma; statusing stores the status byte from the FIFO in the command's private data (when there is a command) and sets msgphase = msg_in; busfreeing calls mesh_done(ms, 1) and returns; disconnecting clears ms->current_req, sets phase = idle, calls mesh_start and returns; any other phase does nothing in the inner switch. For the cases that do not return in the inner switch (selecting, dataing with dma_count zero, statusing, and the default), it then increments ms->phase and calls start_phase(ms). cmd_complete never calls do_abort; the ABORT message is only placed in msgout.

Reviewers all right: original (the idle phase only logs and returns, 1538-1541), r2 (no do_abort call; ABORT is only a message byte, 1548-1550), r15 (selecting, dataing and statusing advance ms->phase and call start_phase, 1617-1618; dataing only when dma_count is 0). name: mpt3sas_base_make_ioc_ready
prose: Function mpt3sas_base_make_ioc_ready(ioc, type) tries to bring the IOC to the READY state and returns 0 or a negative errno. If ioc->pci_error_recovery is set it returns 0 immediately without touching the IOC or checking its state. It reads the IOC state; if it is MPI2_IOC_STATE_RESET it polls once per second (ssleep(1)) for READY and returns -EFAULT if the state is still not READY after 10 polls. If the state is READY it returns 0. If MPI2_DOORBELL_USED is set, or the state is FAULT (printing the fault code), or COREDUMP (waiting for the coredump to finish unless ioc_coredump_loop is already MPT3SAS_COREDUMP_LOOP_DONE), or type is FORCE_BIG_HAMMER, it goes to issue_diag_reset. If the state is OPERATIONAL (and type is not FORCE_BIG_HAMMER) it calls _base_send_ioc_reset with MPI2_FUNCTION_IOC_MESSAGE_UNIT_RESET and a timeout of 15; if that returns 0 it returns 0, otherwise it falls through to issue_diag_reset. Any remaining state also falls through to issue_diag_reset. issue_diag_reset returns the result of _base_diag_reset(ioc), which returns 0 or -EFAULT. This function takes no lock itself; the callee _base_diag_reset takes pci_cfg_access_lock and ioc->hostdiag_unlock_mutex and releases both before returning.

name: _ctl_diag_register_2
prose: Static function _ctl_diag_register_2(ioc, diag_register) registers a diagnostic trace buffer with the firmware and returns a long: 0 or a negative errno. Early returns before any state is changed: if the IOC is not in MPI2_IOC_STATE_OPERATIONAL it sets rc = -EAGAIN and goes to out; if ioc->ctl_cmds.status is not MPT3_CMD_NOT_USED it sets -EAGAIN and goes to out; if the firmware capability check _ctl_diag_capability fails for buffer_type it returns -EPERM; if unique_id is 0, or the buffer is application-owned and not released, it returns -EINVAL. If the buffer type is already registered: when its unique id is the driver's MPT3DIAGBUFFUNIQUEID and its size equals the requested size, then if it is not released the call updates ioc->unique_id[buffer_type] to the new id and returns 0 (rc = 0, goto out, no firmware post), and if it is released the call continues; if its unique id is a different non-driver value and it differs from the request in id or size or is not released it returns -EINVAL; any other registered case returns -EINVAL. If a driver-allocated buffer exists whose id is not MPT3DIAGBUFFUNIQUEID or whose size differs from the request it returns -EINVAL. If requested_buffer_size is not a multiple of 4 it returns -EINVAL. It then gets a smid (none: -EAGAIN via out). From here it modifies state: sets ctl_cmds.status to MPT3_CMD_PENDING, records unique_id, product_specific and diagnostic_flags, narrows diag_buffer_status to the driver-allocated bit, and frees the existing DMA buffer if its size differs from the request; if there is no buffer it allocates one with dma_alloc_coherent (failure: frees the smid and returns -ENOMEM via out). It posts an MPI2_FUNCTION_DIAG_BUFFER_POST request and waits MPT3_IOCTL_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT seconds; if the command did not complete it checks the timeout and goes to the host-reset step (a hard reset FORCE_BIG_HAMMER is issued if issue_reset is set; rc stays 0 in that case); if no valid reply it sets -EFAULT; otherwise if IOCStatus is success it sets MPT3_DIAG_BUFFER_IS_REGISTERED, else it logs and sets -EFAULT. At out: if rc is nonzero and request_data is set it frees the DMA buffer, clears diag_buffer[buffer_type] and the driver-allocated status bit; it then always sets ctl_cmds.status = MPT3_CMD_NOT_USED (including when it got there from the early -EAGAIN path where ctl_cmds.status was in use) and returns rc.

name: _ctl_do_mpt_command
prose: Static function _ctl_do_mpt_command(ioc, karg, mf) executes one user-supplied MPI request through the ioctl interface and returns a long: 0 or a negative errno. Early exits through out (before a message frame is used): ioc->ctl_cmds.status not MPT3_CMD_NOT_USED gives -EAGAIN; a failure of the first setup step gives its error; allocation failure of the request copy gives -ENOMEM; a data_sge_offset beyond the request size or an invalid size gives -EINVAL; a failed copy of the request from user space gives -EFAULT. For MPI2_FUNCTION_SCSI_TASK_MGMT it takes a task-management smid (none: -EAGAIN), otherwise a normal smid. For SCSI I/O style requests an invalid device handle frees the smid and gives -EINVAL. It allocates DMA-coherent data_out (copying from user, -ENOMEM or -EFAULT on failure) and data_in buffers (-ENOMEM on failure), freeing the smid on each of those failures. Then it switches on the MPI function: MCTP passthrough (-EINVAL if the IOC lacks the capability), NVMe encapsulated (-EINVAL without pcie_sg_lookup or when the device removal is in progress), SCSI IO and RAID passthrough, task management (set the task mid, fails and returns via out if _ctl_set_task_mid fails; -EINVAL when device removal is in progress), SMP passthrough (-EINVAL if data_out is NULL in the case checked), SATA passthrough (-EINVAL when device removal is in progress), FW_DOWNLOAD (for an ATTO vendor id it sets ret = -EPERM and leaves the switch without building or submitting the request; other adapters fall through to FW_UPLOAD), FW_UPLOAD, TOOLBOX, SAS_IO_UNIT_CONTROL and a default case, each building the SG list and queuing the smid with put_smid_default. After the switch it waits for completion for max(karg.timeout, MPT3_IOCTL_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT) seconds, clears the TM flag or the link-reset flags as applicable, and if the command did not complete it calls mpt3sas_check_cmd_timeout and goes to issue_host_reset (note this wait is also reached after the ATTO FW_DOWNLOAD branch, where nothing was submitted). On completion it copies out data_in (-ENODATA on copy failure), the reply (-ENODATA on failure) and sense data (-ENODATA on failure). If issue_reset is set it sets ret = -ENODATA and issues a task management reset or a FORCE_BIG_HAMMER hard reset. At out it releases the pcie_device reference, frees the data_in and data_out DMA buffers and the request copy, sets ioc->ctl_cmds.status = MPT3_CMD_NOT_USED (also on the early -EAGAIN exit) and returns ret.

name: _scsih_probe
prose: Static function _scsih_probe(pdev, id) is the PCI probe of the mpt3sas driver; it returns 0, -ENODEV, a positive 1, or the error from scsi_add_host. It returns -ENODEV when hba_mpi_version is 0, when hbas_to_enumerate is 1 and the version is not MPI2_VERSION, when hbas_to_enumerate is 2 and the version is not MPI25 or MPI26, for an unknown hba_mpi_version, or when scsi_host_alloc fails. For MPI2 it disables L0s link state, allocates the host with the mpt2sas template, sets version and multipath fields by device id; for MPI25/MPI26 it allocates the host with the mpt3sas template and, by device id, sets generation flags: the INVALID0 and INVALID1 3816/3916 device ids log that the HBA is invalid or tampered and return 1 (after the host allocation, without releasing the host here); the secure-mode ids log and continue. It then links the ioc into the global list under gioc_lock, initialises the mutexes, spinlocks and list heads, applies the max_sectors limits (clamped for out-of-range module values) and the protection mask, creates the firmware event workqueue (failure: rv = -ENODEV, goto out_thread_fail), calls mpt3sas_base_attach (nonzero: rv = -ENODEV, goto out_attach_fail), sets the number of hw queues and host tagset values, and calls scsi_add_host; if that returns nonzero it goes to out_add_shost_fail. On success it calls scsi_scan_host and mpt3sas_setup_debugfs and returns 0. The failure labels run in sequence: out_add_shost_fail calls mpt3sas_base_detach; out_attach_fail destroys the firmware event workqueue; out_thread_fail removes the ioc from the global list under gioc_lock and calls scsi_host_put(shost); then it returns rv.

name: scsih_sdev_init
prose: Static function scsih_sdev_init(sdev) is the per-LUN init hook of the mpt3sas SCSI host template; it returns 0 or -ENOMEM. It kzallocs an MPT3SAS_DEVICE (failure: returns -ENOMEM with nothing else changed). It stores the lun and MPT_DEVICE_FLAGS_INIT, takes the MPT3SAS_TARGET from scsi_target(sdev)->hostdata, increments its num_luns, links the device to it, stores the new structure in sdev->hostdata, and sets sdev->no_uld_attach = 1 when the target has MPT_TARGET_FLAGS_RAID_COMPONENT. If the target channel is RAID_CHANNEL it takes raid_device_lock (irqsave), looks the raid device up by id and channel and, if found, stores sdev in raid_device->sdev, then releases the lock. If the channel is PCIE_CHANNEL it takes pcie_device_lock, finds the PCIe device by WWID, sets pcie_device->starget when it is NULL, drops the reference taken by the lookup and releases the lock; otherwise, when the target is not a volume (MPT_TARGET_FLAGS_VOLUME clear), it takes sas_device_lock, finds the SAS device by address and port, sets sas_device->starget when it is NULL, drops the lookup reference and releases the lock. It then returns 0.

name: mpt3sas_transport_port_add
prose: Function mpt3sas_transport_port_add(ioc, handle, sas_address, hba_port) creates the SAS transport port and remote phy for a device and returns the new struct _sas_port or NULL. It returns NULL at once if hba_port is NULL or the kzalloc of the _sas_port fails. It finds the sas_node under sas_node_lock; every failure below goes to out_fail unless noted. Failures: no sas_node; _transport_set_identify fails for the handle; the remote device type is SAS_PHY_UNUSED; for a matching phy on the HBA a virtual phy lookup returns none; no phy of the node matched the remote address and hba_port (num_phys is 0); for a SAS end device no sas_device is found; sas_node->parent_dev is NULL; sas_port_alloc_num returns NULL or sas_port_add fails (in the sas_port_add failure case sas_port_delete is not called). Then it allocates the rphy (sas_end_device_alloc for an end device, else sas_expander_alloc); NULL goes to out_delete_port, as does a failing sas_rphy_add (after sas_rphy_free). On success it drops the sas_device reference taken for end devices (this put happens only on the success path, so the failure returns after the sas_device lookup do not drop it), stores the rphy in the port, adds the port to sas_node->sas_port_list under sas_node_lock, reads the manufacturer report for expanders and returns the port. out_delete_port calls sas_port_delete(port) and falls into out_fail, which removes the phys from the port's phy_list, kfree's the _sas_port and returns NULL.

name: mpt3sas_setup_direct_io
prose: Function mpt3sas_setup_direct_io(ioc, scmd, raid_device, mpi_request) tries to turn a WarpDrive volume I/O into a direct I/O to one physical drive; it returns void. It returns without changes when the opcode is not READ_10, WRITE_10, READ_16 or WRITE_16. It reads the LBA from the CDB copy in mpi_request (32-bit big endian for the 10-byte commands, 64-bit for the 16-byte ones) and computes the I/O size in blocks as scsi_bufflen(scmd) shifted by raid_device->block_exponent. It returns without changes if v_lba + io_size - 1 exceeds raid_device->max_lba, or if the I/O crosses a stripe boundary (stripe_off + io_size > stripe_sz, with stripe_off = v_lba & (stripe_sz - 1)). Otherwise it computes the column as the remainder of (v_lba >> stripe_exponent) divided by raid_device->num_pds (using sector_div, and there is no check here that num_pds is nonzero), sets mpi_request->DevHandle to raid_device->pd_handle[column], rewrites the LBA in the CDB copy (the low 32 bits for 10-byte commands, all 64 bits for 16-byte ones) to the physical LBA, and sets st->direct_io = 1. scmd->cmnd itself is not modified.

name: mvs_64xx_init
prose: Static function mvs_64xx_init(mvi) initialises a Marvell 64xx SAS controller and returns 0 or the error from the chip reset. If the PCI revision is 0 it sets MVF_PHY_PWR_FIX. For a non-SOC part it shows PCIe usage and calls mvs_64xx_chip_reset; if that returns nonzero the function returns that value immediately, before any other setup. For a SOC part it adjusts the PHY control register instead. It then reads the control register and clears the reset bit if set, and on a non-SOC part updates PCI config registers PCR_DEV_CTRL, PCR_PHY_CTL and PCR_PHY_CTL2; on SOC parts it toggles link reset with two 100 ms sleeps. It calls mvs_64xx_phy_hacks, sets the CMD_PHY_MODE_21 value, and for each of the chip's n_phy phys it programs the SAS address (big-endian), enables transmit, hard-resets the phy, sleeps 500 ms and detects the port type. On SOC parts it writes fixed values to registers 0x000-0x01c. For each phy it clears PHYEV_SIG_FIS in the port irq status, writes the port irq mask, sleeps 100 ms and calls mvs_update_phyinfo. It then writes the control (endian bits), PCS command, interrupt coalescing and interrupt mask registers, and returns 0. The function sleeps (msleep) so must run in process context; it allocates and frees nothing and takes no locks.

name: myrs_enable_mmio_mbox
prose: Static function myrs_enable_mmio_mbox(cs, enable_mbox_fn) enables the memory mailbox interface of a MYRS controller and returns true on success and false on failure. It sets the DMA mask to 64 bits, falling back to 32 bits; if both fail it returns false. It allocates a temporary command mailbox with dma_alloc_coherent (NULL: returns false). Then, with status initialised to MYRS_STATUS_FAILED, it allocates in order: the command mailbox array (cmd_mbox_size bytes, address cs->cmd_mbox_addr), the status mailbox array, the firmware status buffer (fwstat_buf), cs->ctlr_info (kzalloc) and cs->event_buf (kzalloc); on any of these failing it goes to out_free. If all succeed it records first/last/next/prev mailbox pointers in cs, fills the temporary mailbox with an MYRS_CMD_OP_IOCTL / MYRS_IOCTL_SET_MEM_MBOX command and calls enable_mbox_fn(base, mbox_addr), whose result becomes status. out_free frees only the temporary mailbox (dma_free_coherent), logs a message if status is not MYRS_STATUS_SUCCESS, and returns whether status == MYRS_STATUS_SUCCESS. The buffers stored in cs (command and status mailboxes, fwstat_buf, ctlr_info, event_buf) are not freed by this function in either the success or the failure case, so on failure the earlier allocations stay recorded in cs for the caller to release.

name: nsp32_analyze_sdtr
prose: Static function nsp32_analyze_sdtr(SCpnt) processes a received SDTR (synchronous transfer request) message and returns void. It reads the period from msginbuf[3] and the offset from msginbuf[4] for data->cur_target. Case A, target->sync_flag has SDTR_INITIATOR (we sent the SDTR and this is the reply): it clears SDTR_INITIATOR and sets SDTR_DONE first; then, if the offset exceeds SYNC_OFFSET, or the period is below synct[0].period_num, or nsp32_search_period_entry returns a negative entry, it goes to reject; if the offset equals ASYNC_OFFSET it goes to async; otherwise it calls nsp32_set_sync_entry(entry, offset) and falls to the common end. Case B (the target started the negotiation): it sets SDTR_INITIATOR, clamps the offset to SYNC_OFFSET and the period to synct[0].period_num, looks up the period entry, and if the offset is ASYNC_OFFSET or the entry is negative it calls nsp32_set_async and queues an SDTR reply with period 0 and ASYNC_OFFSET (nsp32_build_sdtr); otherwise it calls nsp32_set_sync_entry and queues an SDTR reply with the clamped period and offset. Both cases then set target->period to the (possibly clamped) get_period and return. The reject label calls nsp32_build_reject (queues a message reject) and then falls into the async label; the async label calls nsp32_set_async and sets target->period = 0, and returns.

Reviewers: original right (the target-initiated path exists and differs, 2301-2327); r2 right (ASYNC_OFFSET in the reply goes to async, not reject, 2261-2266); r15 wrong: in the target-initiated async case the code does queue an SDTR reply (nsp32_build_sdtr(SCpnt, 0, ASYNC_OFFSET), 2322) and target->period is set to the clamped get_period at 2329, not to 0 (period 0 is only set at the async label, reached from the initiator branch or after reject). name: nspintr
prose: Static function nspintr(irq, dev_id) is the interrupt handler of the NSP PCMCIA SCSI adapter and returns IRQ_NONE or IRQ_HANDLED. It returns IRQ_NONE if dev_id or its host is NULL, or if after disabling the adapter interrupt the status register is 0xff or has no bit in IRQSTATUS_MASK (it then re-enables with IRQCONTROL 0). Otherwise it reads the bus monitor phase, and the IRQ phase when IRQSTATUS_SCSI is set (else 0), clears the timer count if it was nonzero, and returns IRQ_HANDLED early in these cases: a timer-only interrupt with SelectionTimeOut == 0 (after clearing the timer); a SCSI reset interrupt (it re-initialises the hardware, resets the bus and completes the current command, if any, with DID_RESET); no current command (hardware init and bus reset); a reselect interrupt (calls nsp_reselected); a SCSI interrupt with neither phase change nor bus free. For the current command it switches on scsi_pointer->phase: PH_SELSTART with BSY clear either times out the command with DID_TIME_OUT once SelectionTimeOut reaches NSP_SELTIMEOUT or increments it and restarts the timer, and with BSY set moves to PH_SELECTED and returns; PH_RESELECT without message-in phase completes the command with DID_ABORT; other phases return if neither the SCSI nor the FIFO interrupt bit is set. If the phase is message in or out and a latched bus free occurred, it completes the command with DID_OK when the last message was COMMAND_COMPLETE (and returns in both cases). If the bus monitor phase is 0 it completes the command with DID_ERROR. Otherwise it dispatches on the bus phase: COMMAND (needs REQ, otherwise returns; sends the CDB), DATA_OUT and DATA_IN (programmed I/O), STATUS (reads the status byte), MESSAGE_OUT (needs REQ, otherwise restarts the timer; builds an IDENTIFY and possibly an SDTR message and sends it), MESSAGE_IN (needs REQ, otherwise restarts the timer; reads the message, analyses SDTR when negotiation is not yet done and records the last message), and SELECT or any other phase (nothing). It returns IRQ_HANDLED at the end; the timer_out path calls nsp_start_timer and returns IRQ_HANDLED.

name: pm8001_mpi_msg_free_set
prose: Function pm8001_mpi_msg_free_set(pm8001_ha, pMsg, circularQ, bc) releases a consumed outbound IOMB and returns u32 0 on both paths shown. It computes the header address msgHeader = pMsg - sizeof(struct mpi_msg_hdr) and the expected header address base_virt + consumer_idx * iomb_size of the outbound queue. If they differ it logs, re-reads the producer index from pi_virt into circularQ->producer_index and returns 0 without advancing consumer_idx or writing the consumer index to the hardware. If they match it advances consumer_idx by bc modulo PM8001_MPI_QUEUE, writes the new consumer index to the controller with pm8001_cw32(ci_pci_bar, ci_offset), re-reads the producer index into circularQ->producer_index, logs the CI and PI and returns 0. It takes no lock.

name: mpi_sata_completion
prose: Static function mpi_sata_completion(pm8001_ha, piomb) completes a SATA I/O from a completion IOMB and returns void. It decodes the status, tag and param from the IOMB, takes the ccb from pm8001_ha->ccb_info[tag], its task t and device. If there is no task it frees the ccb with pm8001_ccb_free and returns. If the device exists and the task, its lldd_task or its dev is NULL it returns without completing. For a failure status other than success, overflow and a few others it may copy the bytes of the register (D2H) FIS into the task's status buffer, depending on whether the device's parent is an expander. It then switches on the status code: each case sets the task status (ts->resp and ts->stat, and for open-reject cases open_rej_reason) and, for most of them when the device pointer is set, decrements pm8001_dev->running_req; IO_SUCCESS with param 0 reports a good status and otherwise builds the SATA response from the FIS (a normal, DMA or NCQ response depending on the task); the IO_OPEN_CNX_ERROR_IT_NEXUS_LOSS, IO_OPEN_CNX_ERROR_BAD_DESTINATION, IO_OPEN_CNX_ERROR_STP_RESOURCES_BUSY, IO_DS_NON_OPERATIONAL and IO_DS_IN_ERROR cases check t->uldd_task: when it is NULL they free the ccb task with pm8001_ccb_task_free_done and return immediately (skipping the completion below), otherwise they continue. After the switch it takes t->task_state_lock, clears SAS_TASK_STATE_PENDING and sets SAS_TASK_STATE_DONE, and, if SAS_TASK_STATE_ABORTED is set, unlocks and calls pm8001_ccb_task_free; otherwise it unlocks and calls pm8001_ccb_task_free_done. The per-status result codes in the individual cases were not each re-verified.

name: pm80xx_get_non_fatal_dump
prose: Function pm80xx_get_non_fatal_dump(cdev, attr, buf) is a sysfs show handler that returns the non-fatal firmware dump in chunks of text and returns a byte count or -EINVAL. If pm8001_ha->controller_fatal_error is set it logs and returns -EINVAL without writing to buf. Otherwise it increments non_fatal_count; if the result is 1 (first call of a dump sequence): for chip_8001 it writes 'Not supported for SPC controller' into pm8001_ha->forensic_info.data_buf.direct_data (not into buf) and returns 0 (non_fatal_count stays incremented); otherwise it programs the dump table (low and high DMA address of the forensic region, SYSFS_OFFSET length, handshake RDY, accumulated length 0) and resets forensic_preserved_accumulated_transfer and non_fatal_read_length to 0. It reads the total length from the table, clears the table status, rings the NONFATAL_DUMP doorbell and busy-polls up to 2 seconds for the doorbell bit to clear, then up to 2 seconds for a nonzero table status. If the status is 0, MPI_FATAL_EDUMP_TABLE_STAT_DMA_FAILED, or greater than MPI_FATAL_EDUMP_TABLE_STAT_NF_SUCCESS_DONE, it sets non_fatal_read_length = 0, writes the word 0xFFFFFFFF to buf, resets non_fatal_count to 0 and returns the number of bytes written. Else if the status is MPI_FATAL_EDUMP_TABLE_STAT_NF_SUCCESS_MORE_DATA it writes the word 2; else if the status is ..._NF_SUCCESS_DONE or non_fatal_read_length >= total_len it resets non_fatal_read_length to 0, writes the word 4 and resets non_fatal_count to 0 (these two cases are an else-if chain, so only one word is written). Then it reads the accumulated length, computes output_length as accum_len minus forensic_preserved_accumulated_transfer, appends output_length/4 words from the forensic memory to buf, adds output_length to non_fatal_read_length (so after a completion word 4 the field is left equal to output_length, not 0), stores accum_len in forensic_preserved_accumulated_transfer and returns the number of bytes written.

name: mpi_smp_completion
prose: Static function mpi_smp_completion(pm8001_ha, piomb) completes an SMP request from a completion IOMB and returns void. It reads status, tag and param from the IOMB payload, takes the ccb from ccb_info[tag], its task t, status struct ts and device pm8001_dev. If t, t->lldd_task or t->dev is NULL it returns (note ts is computed from t before this test, only as an address). It then switches on the status: IO_SUCCESS sets ts->resp = SAS_TASK_COMPLETE and ts->stat = SAS_SAM_STAT_GOOD, decrements pm8001_dev->running_req when the device is set, and, when smp_exp_mode is SMP_DIRECT, maps the response page and loops over param bytes (reading and logging only; it does not copy them anywhere); IO_ABORTED and IO_OVERFLOW set SAS_ABORTED_TASK and SAS_DATA_OVERRUN and decrement running_req when the device is set; the other statuses set ts->resp = SAS_TASK_COMPLETE with a status such as SAS_PHY_DOWN, SAS_SAM_STAT_BUSY, SAS_OPEN_REJECT (with a reason code), SAS_DEV_NO_RESPONSE or SAS_QUEUE_FULL; the IT-nexus-loss family also calls pm8001_handle_event with IO_OPEN_CNX_ERROR_IT_NEXUS_LOSS; any unrecognised status sets SAS_DEV_NO_RESPONSE. After the switch (there is no early return in the cases) it takes task_state_lock with irqsave, clears SAS_TASK_STATE_PENDING and sets SAS_TASK_STATE_DONE; if SAS_TASK_STATE_ABORTED is set it unlocks and calls pm8001_ccb_task_free (with a debug message); otherwise it unlocks, calls pm8001_ccb_task_free, issues a memory barrier and then calls t->task_done(t).
